title: Ethiopian Berbere Legacy Guide
community: All of Ethiopia — the spice that defines the cuisine
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Berbere Legacy — a tasting guide comparing five regional berbere blends: Standard Berbere (ETH141), Tigrayan Berbere (more chilli-forward with black cumin), Gurage Berbere (with extra korerima), Harari Berbere (Arab spice-influenced), and modern Café Berbere (smoky). The spice that defines the cuisine.
longDesc: Berbere is not one spice but hundreds of family and regional variations — this guide explores five major regional interpretations, demonstrating how the same fundamental spice tradition diversifies across Ethiopia's regions.
ingredients: // Tigrayan version: +1 tsp black cumin (tikur azmud)
// Gurage version: +1 tsp korerima (Ethiopian black cardamom)
// Harari version: -dried chilli, +more cumin and coriander
steps: Make each regional variation by adjusting the standard recipe.
chefTips: The differences between regional berberes are subtle but meaningful — train your palate.
sustainabilityTips: All berbere spices grown in Ethiopia.
healthBenefits: Berbere is among the most antioxidant-rich spice blends in the world.
culturalNote: Berbere is the signature of Ethiopian cooking and the recipe every Ethiopian family guards — the specific ratios, the roasting depth, the choice of chillies. No two family berberes are identical. This variation is what makes Ethiopian cooking alive.
